risks.note: Travel activity during the year was impacted by geopolitical tensions and the West Asian conflict, which resulted in deferment of travel decisions and softer travel momentum; management cites geopolitical tensions, particularly in West Asia, as a key monitorable for the sector's near-term outlook.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia disrupting travel demand

risks.note: Supply-side disruption and elevated energy prices raise the risk of near-term inflationary pressures while weighing on private consumption and investor sentiment; global inflation is estimated to rise in 2026 primarily on higher energy and food prices — a direct pressure on discretionary travel spend.
risks.risk: Elevated energy prices and inflation pressure on discretionary consumption

risks.note: Management flags elevated travel costs together with macroeconomic uncertainties as key monitorables for the sector's near-term outlook, alongside risks from persistent trade frictions.
risks.risk: Elevated travel costs and macroeconomic uncertainty

risks.note: Travel activity was impacted by aviation-related disruptions during the year and domestic air passenger traffic grew only modestly Y-o-Y; the outlook for international tourism is explicitly tied to improved air connectivity.
risks.risk: Aviation-related disruption and dependence on air connectivity

risks.note: Adverse weather events are named among the external developments that intermittently affected demand and deferred travel decisions during the year.
risks.risk: Adverse weather events affecting travel demand

risks.note: Per Horwath HTL, branded hotel room supply expanded 7.8% Y-o-Y, with nearly 41% of the new supply added in 2025 pertaining to the premium (upscale and above) segment — the segment in which the Company competes — and the majority added outside the top ten markets.
risks.risk: New branded room supply, concentrated in the premium segment

sk.overview: The overnight ocean and coastal cruise industry in India is a nascent, high-growth segment of cruise tourism. Per the issuer-commissioned CRISIL Report (May 2026), the domestic market was valued at approximately Rs 8,301 million in Fiscal 2025 (up from Rs 5,764 million in Fiscal 2020, ~8% CAGR) but is estimated to have declined ~12% to Rs 7,325 million in Fiscal 2026 amid macro/fuel/geopolitical headwinds, before a projected sharp expansion.
